name: Extract a term/relation graph from a how-to transcript with domain lexicons
goal: Parse an English how-to transcript into a JSON graph of useful data. Nodes are concepts, modules, params, values, tools, procedure steps, and repeated phrases. Edges are sets (param -> value), affects (mod source -> target), precedes (step order), part-of (param -> module, module -> tool), and mentions (step -> term), each with timestamped evidence quotes. Matching uses domain lexicons for synth/sound design, Blender, crypto tooling, side hustle, and drone/splat capture, plus bigram/trigram collocation mining for terms the lexicon doesn't know. Delta vs generic keyword or knowledge-graph skills (understand-anything): deterministic and stdlib-only, unit-aware value attachment (dB -> slope/level, semitones -> pitch, voices -> unison), and evidence-grounded edges built for gap checking against a skill catalog.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.description: synth|blender|crypto|sidehustle|drone (auto-detected by lexicon hit count if omitted)

outputs.name: graph
outputs.description: raw/<id>/graph.json (schema yt-knowledge-graph/v1): nodes[], edges[], stats, domain_scores, source provenance (route, translated)

constraints: Transcript source is YouTube's Show transcript panel text (info section -> Transcript); say 'transcript', not 'captions'. Caption-file transports (.srt/.vtt) are only used internally and deleted.
Never invent transcript text, steps, or settings; every downstream fact must trace to a transcript timestamp.
No Whisper/ASR on the audio unless Matt explicitly asks; the router may only FLAG it as a last resort.

Evidence quotes are verbatim transcript slices (max 160 chars) and stay local (raw/ is gitignored for transcript text; graph.json is too). Only {video_id, t} references go to the public knowledge graph.
Prefer precision: short ambiguous aliases (am, live, q, time, note) are excluded from lexicons; values attach only to params/modules allowed for that unit (lexicon unit_targets).
Collocation 'phrase' nodes are suggestions for lexicon growth, not facts; they never create skill steps on their own.

steps.action: Load panel segments (skip '#' header lines, strip [Music]-style markers) and merge them into about 240-character windows so a sentence-like unit holds a full instruction.
Detect the domain by counting lexicon matches for every lexicon over the full text; use the best one unless --domain is given. Record domain_scores.

In each window, match aliases longest-first with word boundaries and make module/param/tool/concept nodes. Add param -> module part-of from the lexicon, and module -> tool part-of when both are mentioned in the same window.
steps.expect: Term nodes with counts and evidence

steps.action: Find values (number or number word + unit: Hz, kHz, ms, s, %, dB, semitones, cents, voices, octaves, bars). Attach each to the noun right after it when within 3 chars ('24 dB slope'), else to the nearest preceding allowed param/module within 70 chars. Emit a value node and a sets edge.
steps.expect: e.g. unison sets '5 voices', filter_slope sets '24 db'

steps.action: For mod sources (LFO, envelope, velocity, macro, mod wheel, keytrack, random), emit affects -> target when a connector (to/onto/controls/modulates/assign/route) sits between them within 60 chars, skipping envelope -> attack-style part-of pairs.
steps.expect: e.g. envelope affects cutoff, macro affects mix

steps.action: Mark a window as a step when it has an action verb plus a step cue or 2+ terms. Link steps with precedes and steps to terms with mentions. Mine bigram/trigram collocations (frequency >= 3, PMI-ranked, stopword-trimmed) as phrase nodes. Write graph.json with stats.

verification: graph.json stats.nodes > 0 and stats.edges > 0 for a usable how-to
Every node and edge has at least one evidence {t, quote}
Re-running on the same transcript gives an identical graph (deterministic)
